fact: The World Bank blog says the Gambia Social Registry (GamSR), covering 203,022 households in 40 of 43 districts, underpinned the Nafa Quick COVID-19 response (78,422 households) and the Nafa cash-transfer programme (16,966 households), and is also used by the National Disaster Management Agency, the ROOTS project and the World Food Programme; no event date is given, so the publication date is used.
source_slug: 2024-04-23 The Gambia Social Registry - A Success Story in Systems Building

fact: The World Bank's November 2025 status report on the RISE project says complementary systems strengthening, including social registry enhancements and interoperability efforts, progressed, without naming the systems linked.

The World Bank framework says Gambian social protection agencies operate in silos with little information shared across them, and that the Department of Social Welfare and Community Development hold no functional information systems; the date is the document's published year, as it gives none for the finding (its missions ran November 2017 to May 2018).
